The microstructure of the interstitial-free steel reference is shown in Fig. S1 of the Supplementary materials (not reproduced in the main text).
Specific modulus (E/ρ) of the IF steel is approximately 26.5 GPa·g⁻¹·cm³, read from the black 'IF steel' star in the property map of Fig. 3(c).
The product of specific yield strength and uniform elongation (SYS × UE) for the IF steel is approximately 5–6 MPa·g⁻¹·cm³, read from the black 'IF steel' star in Fig. 3(c).

A direct comparison between the conventional Fe-TiB2 steel (orange) and interstitial-free steel (black) reference curves reveals that any strength increment due solely to ceramic additions would cause a drastic loss in ductility.
The interstitial-free steel is used as the black tensile reference curve in both Fig. 3(a) and the FE-simulated Fig. 11(a), serving as the α-ferrite matrix benchmark without TiB2.
In the FE simulation the simulated interstitial-free steel curve reaches about 460 MPa at ~0.18 true strain (Fig. 11(a) description).
